scope: Hostile causation audit of whether Francisco de Borja Rodríguez-Batllori Laffitte, as Administrador Concursal of Luchy Playa Blanca, S.L.U., materially interfered with, destabilised or caused changes in owner-side legal representation from the pre-Concurso period through current counsel.

method.publicNarrativeIntegratedMandate: Public wording must combine accepted/billed scope, AC act, professional response or limit, result, deterioration/transition, client position and contrary evidence. A formal exit reason is not an exhaustive finding about prior AC effect or mandate performance.
method.privateSourceBoundary: Underlying private Gmail and Drive material remains in connected source systems. This file preserves public-safe source descriptions, dates, evidential states and analytical consequences only.
method.negativeEvidenceRule: No evidence located is not proof of non-existence or non-occurrence.
method.counterfactualQuestion: Would the engagement probably have ended, narrowed or failed to formalise if the identified AC event had not occurred?

causationScale.C0: No identifiable causal connection on the current record.
causationScale.C1: Temporal/background connection only; direct causes point elsewhere.
causationScale.C2: Plausible contributing factor but evidence is incomplete or materially mixed.
causationScale.C3: Materially supported contributing factor to workstream burden, disruption, cost or strategy; not necessarily to exit.
causationScale.C4: Strong evidence of substantial causal contribution to the representation change.
causationScale.C5: Direct contemporaneous evidence that AC conduct caused or materially precipitated the representation change.

overallFindings.proposition: AC conduct or AC-controlled procedural dependencies repeatedly imposed material burdens, constraints, workarounds or additional complexity on several owner-side lawyers.
overallFindings.qualification: The mechanisms and strength vary by lawyer and matter; professional conflict with the AC is not itself proof of misconduct or improper purpose.

overallFindings.proposition: The present record does not establish one exclusive, universal chain in which Borja caused every succession of lawyers, or a deliberate strategy to push all principal lawyers away.
overallFindings.qualification: Formal reasons such as non-payment, strategy/confidence or failed replacement continuity remain material. They must not be used as exhaustive answers to earlier AC impact, mandate effectiveness or cumulative deterioration.

overallFindings.proposition: A continuity asymmetry existed: the Administrador Concursal remained institutionally continuous while owner-side legal teams and mandates changed over a prolonged proceeding.
overallFindings.qualification: The asymmetry is descriptively important but does not by itself prove that the AC caused the turnover.

overallFindings.proposition: Unpaid or disputed professional fees are a recurring, independently documented attrition factor that must be retained in the integrated mandate history.
overallFindings.qualification: This factor is particularly clear for Garrigues/Cuatrecasas/Daniel Jiménez/Luis Miguel López and other advisers. It is neither suppressed nor treated as an automatic rebuttal of prior AC impact or alleged protection failures.

overallFindings.proposition: Direct evidence that Borja deliberately intended to isolate, discourage or push away a lawyer has not been located in the present pass.
overallFindings.qualification: Objective impact, knowledge/foreseeability and intent must remain separate propositions.

engagementAssessments.clientMatter: LPB and connected pre-Concurso / litigation / Bankia work
engagementAssessments.documentedAlternativeCause: Contemporaneous client-side fee/value dispute immediately around the transition to new representation.
engagementAssessments.acSpecificFinding: No current source located showing Borja caused the Garrigues transition.
engagementAssessments.counterEvidence: The transition occurred at the birth of the Concurso while the fee/value dispute is directly documented.
engagementAssessments.openQuestion: Recover the exact engagement-end/venia and earliest AC appointment/communication chain.

engagementAssessments.documentedAlternativeCause: Client-initiated substitution framed contemporaneously as mutual loss of confidence; Parrilla accepted the decision as best for both sides.
engagementAssessments.acSpecificFinding: AC involvement is material to the later fee/handover dispute but is not established as the cause of the initial replacement.
engagementAssessments.counterEvidence: The outgoing lawyer expressly accepted the substitution and granted venia.
engagementAssessments.openQuestion: Separate ordinary concursal fee administration from any independently provable interference with handover or successor work.

engagementAssessments.documentedAlternativeCause: Formal 26 May 2020 renunciation correspondence expressly attributes inability to continue to non-payment of fees for more than two years.
engagementAssessments.acSpecificFinding: The 2018/Q1-2019 proformas and 2019 correspondence document a broad finance/insolvency protection programme and IA-facing work across the liquidation plan, information, standing, sales/Registry, Acosta Matos/Community, ONA, financing, security and exit. April 2019 correspondence also records entity-specific mandate limits and conditioned responses when Gil/LPB required classification and CAM/IA protection.
engagementAssessments.clientPosition: Gil/Patricia allege that the firm and its partners did not fully deploy the protective architecture billed for and that IA conduct materially affected its efficacy. This is not an adjudicated professional-negligence finding.
engagementAssessments.counterEvidence: Cuatrecasas obtained favourable October 2019 orders, including rejection of the IA exclusion request, then granted venia promptly and assisted the successor handover.
engagementAssessments.openQuestion: Map each billed protective task to the client/entity, IA event, requested response, professional boundary, result and loss alleged; obtain the complete engagement and invoice/payment file.

engagementAssessments.acSpecificFinding: Repeated AC-related disputes and evidential work are documented, but Cristo persisted across successive teams.
engagementAssessments.counterEvidence: Long-running continuation is affirmative counterevidence to a universal push-away theory.
engagementAssessments.openQuestion: Map exact client-specific mandates and periods rather than treating his role as one continuous generic engagement.

engagementAssessments.documentedAlternativeCause: Formal 23 June 2020 resignation identifies strategy divergence, disagreement over control of legal strategy, and unpaid agreed fees.
engagementAssessments.acSpecificFinding: Direct June 2020 friction with the AC is documented, including concern about work/fee negotiations becoming tied to the position of JT/AC and disagreement over who should channel information/questions to the AC.
engagementAssessments.counterEvidence: The lawyer's formal resignation does not identify Borja as a reason for leaving.
engagementAssessments.openQuestion: Determine whether AC friction materially accelerated a resignation already independently supported by strategy and fee causes.

engagementAssessments.clientMatter: Proposed/accepted successor work concerning LPB/Concurso recovery and AC removal
engagementAssessments.acSpecificFinding: The team operationally accepted the transition, requested venia/information and analysed AC removal and recovery routes, but later correspondence records that formal personation did not occur.

engagementAssessments.openQuestion: Recover retainer/fee/conflict/onboarding/decision correspondence explaining why DWF/RCD did not formally substitute despite active July 2020 work.

engagementAssessments.professional: Luis Miguel López Gómez / López Castelo
engagementAssessments.documentedAlternativeCause: Repeated renunciation communications focus on years of unpaid work, the failure of replacement lawyers to formally appear, and the need to avoid indefensión.
engagementAssessments.acSpecificFinding: Luis Miguel independently recommended AC removal/liability review and described AC-controlled conditions affecting proposed actions, including swap litigation, but continued acting for years despite these conflicts.
engagementAssessments.counterEvidence: He remained active through 2023 and filed the LPB calificación appeal despite earlier matter-specific/general renunciation communications.
engagementAssessments.openQuestion: Reconstruct each renunciation by matter and determine the precise reason replacement counsel failed to take over.

engagementAssessments.professional: Javier Sixto and Estefanía Sixto-Seijas / Sixto Abogados
engagementAssessments.clientMatter: Aweswell/LPB and connected Concurso, appellate and recovery work
engagementAssessments.acSpecificFinding: The September 2023 LPB swap/power episode is a strong example of objective workstream disruption: the AC's position on power/authority required immediate redesign of standing and filing strategy and created risk of inadmission/dismissal.
engagementAssessments.counterEvidence: Sixto did not withdraw; it adapted, continued, and in 2025-2026 actively litigated separation/removal of the AC, including appeals and oppositions.
engagementAssessments.openQuestion: Quantify added procedural work/cost and separate legitimate fiduciary verification by the AC from any provable overreach.

engagementAssessments.clientMatter: Current Matkator/ETJ, criminal and connected recovery work
engagementAssessments.acSpecificFinding: Current work includes AC-related subject matter, but this pass has not located a direct Borja-to-Carlos interaction establishing interference with Carlos's mandate.
engagementAssessments.counterEvidence: Carlos remains actively engaged and has accepted further matters in 2026.
engagementAssessments.openQuestion: Continue monitoring direct AC interactions and any practical effect on current filings or access to information.

engagementAssessments.clientMatter: Specialist/legal support around late-2018 and later work
engagementAssessments.documentedAlternativeCause: Contemporaneous correspondence directly links willingness/capacity to continue to unpaid invoices.
engagementAssessments.acSpecificFinding: No current evidence attributes reduced involvement to Borja.
engagementAssessments.openQuestion: Classify whether this was a retained engagement, specialist consultation or matter-specific support.

materialEvents.event: Fee/handover negotiations and direct AC-lawyer friction during Aweswell/LPB representation transition.
materialEvents.effect: Added pressure and professional disagreement; Daniel objected to dependence of his fee position on AC/JT negotiations.
materialEvents.strongestDefence: The AC was managing matters arising within a concurso and enforcing role boundaries; Daniel's formal resignation identifies independent strategy and payment causes.

materialEvents.effect: Sixto had to redesign standing/filing strategy and address risk that the action could fail for lack of debtor authority/power.
materialEvents.strongestDefence: The AC was entitled or obliged to verify that an action for the debtor matched the previously authorised/accepted claim and was in the estate's interest.

materialEvents.event: Active adversarial proceedings concerning separation/removal of the AC and related appellate steps.
materialEvents.effect: Significant procedural workload and direct opposition.
materialEvents.strongestDefence: Adversarial opposition to removal is an ordinary exercise of procedural rights and does not establish interference with counsel.

safeCurrentConclusion: Across several independent legal teams, the record supports treating AC-controlled procedural and authority dependencies as a recurring material influence on owner-side representation. Each mandate must be described as an integrated history of billed scope, IA conduct, professional response or limit, result and later transition. Formal exit reasons remain relevant without deciding the prior AC effect or mandate effectiveness. Exclusive-cause, deliberate-intent and professional-liability findings remain unproved unless specifically adjudicated.

publicationGate.reason: Internal causation grades are evidential controls, not suitable public characterisations. Public wording may state actor-specific documented practical effects and attributed client allegations, but must integrate mandate scope, response, results, formal transition evidence and counterevidence; it may not imply exclusive causation, intent or adjudicated professional liability without stronger proof.
